rows.title: Obtain and maintain the right authority

topics.title: Initial eligibility, examination, application and fee
Producer, adviser, nonresident and business-entity licenses
Viatical licensing; exceptions and temporary authority
License duration, termination, renewal and CE
Producer contract versus appointment; individual versus agency appointment
Solicitation before appointment and appointment after licensing
Appointment notice, cessation, termination and lack of active appointments
Probation, suspension, revocation, denial and nonrenewal
Cease-and-desist orders, penalties and hearing rights

rows.example: A new recruit changes address, receives an appointment and later faces an administrative action. Sort the separate duties and deadlines.
rows.assessment: Identify authority and required next action; use current Maryland deadlines, including criminal prosecution reporting rather than only conviction.

evidence.text: No dedicated published lesson found. Question-bank references are not instructional coverage.

rows.title: Regulate insurers and producer conduct

topics.title: Insurer authorization, forms and claims oversight
Records and permitted work by unlicensed people
Commissions, sharing, fees and compensation exceptions
Fiduciary duties, commingling and trust accounts
False advertising, defamation and false financial statements

rows.example: Compare an honest policy comparison, an unlawful inducement and misuse of a premium check.
rows.assessment: Name the conduct from facts and select the lawful correction; check statutory exceptions instead of teaching blanket bans.

evidence.text: No dedicated published lesson found. Question-bank references are not instructional coverage.

rows.title: Apply Maryland life transaction rules

topics.title: Guaranty corporation purpose, eligibility, limits and advertising restrictions

rows.example: An employee leaves work while another client replaces an old policy. Use separate checklists for each transaction.
rows.assessment: Distinguish conversion from replacement; apply actual state provisions and identify what guaranty protection does not promise.

evidence.text: No dedicated published lesson found. Question-bank references are not instructional coverage.

rows.title: Explain how insurance handles uncertainty
rows.lesson: 01–02 plus next Part 3: risk handling and insurability
rows.example: Daniel compares avoiding a hazard, retaining a cost and transferring financial risk; show the insurer separately transferring risk to another insurer.
rows.assessment: Classify changed scenarios; explain why pooling cannot predict an individual claim. Add missing risk-handling and reinsurance questions.

evidence.text: Parts 1–2 explain five risk terms, hazards, pooling, large numbers and adverse selection; 16 formative questions. Risk-handling methods, insurability and reinsurance are incomplete.

rows.title: Identify the insurer and distribution model
rows.lesson: 02 supplement; separate from the existing pooling video

topics.title: Private and governmental insurers and plans

rows.example: One insurer is formed in another state and licensed in Maryland. Separate domicile, authorization and ownership.
rows.assessment: Classify the same insurer on each dimension; avoid treating a financial rating as a guarantee.

evidence.text: No dedicated published lesson found. Question-bank references are not instructional coverage.

rows.title: Recognize agency relationships

topics.title: Insurer as principal and producer as agent

rows.example: A producer makes a promise beyond written authority; determine who created the appearance of authority.
rows.assessment: Choose the authority type and proper producer action from plausible alternatives.

evidence.text: No dedicated published lesson found. Question-bank references are not instructional coverage.

topics.title: Indemnity compared with a stated life benefit

rows.example: Trace application, premium and insurer acceptance, then contrast an ambiguous clause with a clear exclusion.
rows.assessment: Identify the contract element or doctrine; avoid promising that expectations override every clear exclusion.

rows.lesson: 31B: who makes, coordinates or administers rules

topics.title: Interstate insurance product compact and IIPRC role

topics.title: Own-life purchases versus insurance on another

rows.title: Connect protection to personal needs
rows.example: A family needs immediate cash after a death and income through a child’s schooling.
rows.assessment: Identify the purpose without implying every household needs the same product.

evidence.text: Part 1 introduces family income exposure. No complete needs lesson or dedicated needs assessment yet.

topics.title: Chronic illness and terminal illness definitions
Broker, provider, purchaser and viator roles

rows.example: Use fictional income, debts, resources and time horizons in a worksheet with explicit assumptions.
rows.assessment: Calculate a stated need and identify missing facts; do not promise Social Security eligibility or benefit amounts.

evidence.text: No dedicated published lesson found. Question-bank references are not instructional coverage.

rows.title: Match business protection to the loss
rows.example: A business loses an owner versus an essential employee; follow ownership and benefit flows.
rows.assessment: Choose the arrangement, policyowner and beneficiary appropriate to the stated objective.

rows.title: Classify coverage before comparing products

topics.title: Fixed versus variable life and annuity designs

rows.example: Classify a policy on several independent dimensions rather than treating each label as a competing product.
rows.assessment: Identify which guarantees, participation features and regulatory requirements belong to the stated design.

evidence.text: The earlier term/whole-life prototype addresses the temporary/permanent distinction only.

rows.title: Explain premium construction
rows.example: Build a simplified price from mortality, interest and expenses, then compare annual and monthly modes.
rows.assessment: Distinguish an illustrative expected claim cost from an actual premium.

evidence.text: Part 2 distinguishes illustrative expected claims from an actual premium; no premium-construction lesson yet.

rows.title: Handle application through delivery

topics.title: Sales presentations and guaranty advertising restrictions

rows.example: Follow a client’s file from first conversation to delivery, pausing where a missing signature or changed health matters.
rows.assessment: Select the next required action; teach Maryland disclosure timing from current rules, not generic deadlines.

evidence.text: No dedicated published lesson found. Question-bank references are not instructional coverage.

rows.title: Evaluate applications fairly

topics.title: Medical examination, laboratory results and HIV

rows.example: Compare permitted information and classification decisions in several fictional files.
rows.assessment: Identify information sources and legal limits without stereotypes or unsupported denial-rate claims.

evidence.text: Part 2 introduces underwriting as a response to adverse selection; it does not teach the full underwriting workflow.

rows.title: Choose and distinguish term designs
rows.example: Overlay premium and benefit timelines for level, renewable and decreasing term.
rows.assessment: Change duration or renewal facts so students cannot answer from the word term alone.

evidence.text: The term/whole-life prototype teaches basic term duration and lack of cash value, with three comparison questions. Term variants remain incomplete.

rows.title: Distinguish permanent designs
rows.example: Separate premium schedules, cash-value guarantees and investment risk on product cards.
rows.assessment: State product assumptions; do not transfer a whole-life guarantee to every variable or universal design.

evidence.text: The prototype teaches traditional whole-life features. Other permanent designs are not taught.

rows.title: Explain adjustable and universal coverage

rows.example: A policyowner pays less for several months; show charges continuing and possible lapse risk.
rows.assessment: Distinguish flexible payments from guaranteed lifetime coverage without funding.
